Unlike Hive partitioning, there are no rigid subdirectory paths, preventing directory listing lag on cloud storage.
ALTER TABLE CLUSTER BY applies only to newly written or compacted files; no immediate table rewrites needed.
Predictive Optimization in Unity Catalog automates OPTIMIZE runs for Liquid Clustered tables.
use_case: Replacing rigid legacy Hive partitioning on a 10TB transaction table to eliminate small files and accelerate multi-key analytical filters.

title: VACUUM Lifecycle Management & Retention Safety Guards
description: Production storage hygiene guide for Delta Lake VACUUM. Details transaction log retention vs data file retention, safe default thresholds (168 hours), dry run auditing, and concurrent reader safety.
notes: VACUUM deletes physical Parquet data files that are no longer referenced in the Delta log state past retention.
Never reduce retention below 168 hours (7 days) in production to avoid corrupting concurrent active queries.
Time travel queries referencing versions older than the VACUUM retention threshold will fail with FileNotFoundException.
Managed tables under Unity Catalog can leverage automated Predictive Optimization for unattended VACUUM execution.
use_case: Reclaiming petabytes of orphaned storage from daily MERGE and UPDATE operations without corrupting ongoing BI reader queries.

title: Advanced Delta MERGE INTO with Conditional Updates & Schema Evolution
description: Mastering the MERGE INTO statement in Spark SQL. Explores conditional multiple MATCHED clauses, delete tombstones, schema evolution on upsert, and minimizing write amplification with deletion vectors.
code:
-- Enable schema evolution on merge
SET spark.databricks.delta.schema.autoMerge.enabled = true;

-- Advanced MERGE with multiple conditional MATCHED and NOT MATCHED clauses
MERGE INTO silver.customers AS target
USING staging.customer_updates AS source
ON target.customer_id = source.customer_id

-- Clause 1: Hard delete requested by GDPR right-to-be-forgotten
WHEN MATCHED AND source.op_type = 'DELETE' THEN
  DELETE

-- Clause 2: Standard update with audit timestamp checking
WHEN MATCHED AND source.updated_at > target.updated_at THEN
  UPDATE SET
    target.name = source.name,
    target.email = source.email,
    target.address = source.address,
    target.phone = source.phone,
    target.updated_at = source.updated_at,
    target.loyalty_tier = source.loyalty_tier

-- Clause 3: Insert new customer records
WHEN NOT MATCHED AND source.op_type != 'DELETE' THEN
  INSERT (customer_id, name, email, address, phone, created_at, updated_at, loyalty_tier)
  VALUES (source.customer_id, source.name, source.email, source.address, source.phone, source.updated_at, source.updated_at, source.loyalty_tier);
notes: Multiple WHEN MATCHED clauses are evaluated in top-to-bottom sequence; the first true predicate is executed.
autoMerge.enabled dynamically adds new columns from source into the target table schema during MERGE execution.
Deletion Vectors (delta.enableDeletionVectors = true) eliminate full Parquet file rewrites for matched DELETE and UPDATE rows.
Adding partition/clustering pruning predicates to the ON clause (e.g. target.txn_date = source.txn_date) drastically reduces scanned files.
use_case: Processing continuous CDC feeds containing inserts, updates, and GDPR user deletions into a conformed customer dimension table.

title: Delta Change Data Feed (CDF) Querying & Incremental Pipelines
description: Enabling and consuming Delta Lake Change Data Feed (CDF). Demonstrates reading row-level mutations (inserts, updates, deletes) via table_changes() across commit versions and timestamps.
code:
-- 1. Enable Change Data Feed on table creation or alteration
ALTER TABLE silver.products SET TBLPROPERTIES (delta.enableChangeDataFeed = true);

-- 2. Inspect table change history
DESCRIBE HISTORY silver.products;

-- 3. Query all changes between version 10 and 15
SELECT 
    product_id,
    product_name,
    unit_price,
    _change_type,
    _commit_version,
    _commit_timestamp
FROM table_changes('silver.products', 10, 15)
ORDER BY _commit_version, _commit_timestamp;

-- 4. Filter only price updates (comparing pre-image vs post-image)
SELECT 
    product_id,
    unit_price,
    _change_type,
    _commit_timestamp
FROM table_changes('silver.products', 10)
WHERE _change_type IN ('update_preimage', 'update_postimage')
ORDER BY product_id, _commit_timestamp;

-- 5. Using CDF as a streaming source in PySpark:
-- spark.readStream.format('delta') \
--   .option('readChangeFeed', 'true') \
--   .option('startingVersion', 10) \
--   .table('silver.products')
notes: _change_type contains: 'insert' (new rows), 'update_preimage' (row before update), 'update_postimage' (row after update), 'delete' (deleted row).
CDF stores change events either within existing data files or as separate lightweight change files in the Delta folder.
Ideal for driving incremental downstream materialized views, audit trails, and syncing search indexes (e.g. Elasticsearch).
CDF queries are bounded by the VACUUM retention period; older change data is purged during vacuum.
use_case: Capturing product catalog price changes incrementally to trigger downstream pricing alert notifications and update search indexes.

title: Higher-Order Functions for Complex Nested JSON & Arrays
description: Transforming complex nested data types (ARRAY, STRUCT, MAP) using Spark SQL higher-order functions (TRANSFORM, FILTER, AGGREGATE, EXISTS) without exploding and re-aggregating rows.
code:
-- Sample nested order data with line items array
WITH raw_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        101 AS order_id,
        'Santosh' AS customer,
        ARRAY(
            NAMED_STRUCT('item', 'Laptop', 'qty', 1, 'price', 1200.0, 'taxable', true),
            NAMED_STRUCT('item', 'Mouse', 'qty', 2, 'price', 25.0, 'taxable', true),
            NAMED_STRUCT('item', 'GiftCard', 'qty', 1, 'price', 50.0, 'taxable', false)
        ) AS items
)
SELECT
    order_id,
    customer,
    
    -- 1. TRANSFORM: Apply function to each element in array (10% discount on items)
    TRANSFORM(items, x -> NAMED_STRUCT('item', x.item, 'discounted_price', ROUND(x.price * 0.9, 2))) AS discounted_items,
    
    -- 2. FILTER: Extract only taxable line items
    FILTER(items, x -> x.taxable = true) AS taxable_items,
    
    -- 3. EXISTS: Check if order contains a high-value item (> $500)
    EXISTS(items, x -> x.price > 500.0) AS has_expensive_item,
    
    -- 4. AGGREGATE: Calculate order gross total directly without explode()
    AGGREGATE(items, 0.0, (total, x) -> total + (x.qty * x.price)) AS order_total_amount
FROM raw_orders;
notes: Higher-order functions evaluate lambda expressions directly over array elements in memory.
Avoids using EXPLODE() which duplicates parent row columns and triggers expensive shuffle and memory allocation.
AGGREGATE(array, zero, merge, finish) performs accumulator folds across array structures efficiently.
TRANSFORM and FILTER are fully optimized by the Catalyst Optimizer and Photon engine.
use_case: Processing nested e-commerce order payloads in Spark SQL without explosive row multiplication and memory pressure.

title: Liquid Clustering DDL & Dynamic Key Restructuring
description: Configuring Delta Lake Liquid Clustering (CLUSTER BY) in Databricks SQL. Replaces static Hive-style directory partitioning and manual Z-ORDERING, allowing dynamic key changes without table rewrites.
code:
-- 1. Create table with Liquid Clustering on high-cardinality keys
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE prod_catalog.silver.sales_transactions (
    txn_id STRING NOT NULL,
    customer_id STRING NOT NULL,
    store_id STRING NOT NULL,
    txn_amount DECIMAL(18, 4) NOT NULL,
    txn_timestamp TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
    txn_date DATE GENERATED ALWAYS AS (CAST(txn_timestamp AS DATE))
)
USING DELTA
CLUSTER BY (customer_id, txn_date) -- Liquid clustering dynamically arranges data across multiple keys
TBLPROPERTIES (
    'delta.autoOptimize.optimizeWrites' = 'true',
    'delta.autoOptimize.autoCompact' = 'true'
);

-- 2. Restructure clustering columns dynamically (zero data rewrite needed)
ALTER TABLE prod_catalog.silver.sales_transactions
CLUSTER BY (store_id, txn_date);

-- 3. Trigger manual clustering compaction
OPTIMIZE prod_catalog.silver.sales_transactions;

-- 4. Inspect clustering metadata
DESCRIBE DETAIL prod_catalog.silver.sales_transactions;
notes: Liquid Clustering replaces Hive partitioning (/year=2026/month=10/) and eliminates the small file problem.
Unlike static partitioning, you can change clustering columns via ALTER TABLE without rewriting historical data.
Optimized for Databricks Runtime 13.3+ LTS and Photon Engine with Predictive I/O.
Supports up to 4 clustering keys; choose columns frequently used in WHERE filters and join predicates.
use_case: Designing modern lakehouse fact tables with billions of rows where query access patterns vary between customer analytics and store-level reporting.

title: QUALIFY Clause for Elegant Top-N Partition Pruning
description: Utilizing the ANSI QUALIFY clause in Spark SQL to filter window function results directly without creating messy nested subqueries or temporary views. Greatly improves query readability and optimization.
code:
-- =============================================================================
-- Identify the Top 3 Highest Value Transactions per Customer in 2026
-- =============================================================================

USE CATALOG prod_catalog;
USE SCHEMA silver;

-- ❌ OLD PATTERN: Required verbose CTE or subquery wrapping
-- WITH ranked AS (
--   SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY txn_amount DESC) as rnk
--   FROM sales_transactions
-- )
-- SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 3;

-- ✅ MODERN QUALIFY PATTERN: Single declarative statement
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    txn_id,
    txn_amount,
    txn_timestamp,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
        PARTITION BY customer_id 
        ORDER BY txn_amount DESC
    ) AS transaction_rank,
    DENSE_RANK() OVER (
        PARTITION BY customer_id 
        ORDER BY txn_amount DESC
    ) AS transaction_dense_rank
FROM sales_transactions
WHERE txn_date >= '2026-01-01'
QUALIFY transaction_rank <= 3
ORDER BY customer_id, transaction_rank;
notes: QUALIFY is evaluated after WHERE and window functions, but before ORDER BY and LIMIT.
Eliminates subqueries and Common Table Expressions (CTEs) previously required to filter on window outputs.
Catalyst optimizer can push window limits into physical Top-K execution operators when paired with QUALIFY.
Supported across Databricks SQL, Snowflake, and Google BigQuery.
use_case: Extracting the top 3 highest-value purchases or latest status updates per customer in executive sales summaries without maintaining nested subquery boilerplate.

title: Relational Matrix Reshaping via PIVOT and UNPIVOT
description: Transforming normalized relational rows into cross-tabulated metric matrices using PIVOT, and normalizing matrix columns back into relational key-value pairs using UNPIVOT.
code:
-- =============================================================================
-- 1. PIVOT: Transpose quarterly revenue metrics by Region
-- =============================================================================
SELECT * FROM (
    SELECT 
        region,
        quarter,
        revenue
    FROM prod_catalog.gold.regional_financials
)
PIVOT (
    SUM(revenue)
    FOR quarter IN ('Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4')
)
ORDER BY region;

-- =============================================================================
-- 2. UNPIVOT: Normalize wide monthly columns back into relational key-value rows
-- =============================================================================
SELECT 
    product_id,
    month_name,
    units_sold
FROM prod_catalog.staging.wide_monthly_forecast
UNPIVOT (
    units_sold FOR month_name IN (
        jan_sales AS 'January',
        feb_sales AS 'February',
        mar_sales AS 'March',
        apr_sales AS 'April'
    )
);
notes: PIVOT requires explicit enumeration of pivot values IN ('Q1', 'Q2', ...) to generate deterministic output schemas.
UNPIVOT replaces complex UNION ALL chains with a single, highly optimized Catalyst physical operator.
Essential for transforming third-party financial spreadsheets into clean 3NF Medallion tables.
Combines seamlessly with GROUP BY to calculate sub-totals alongside pivoted metrics.
use_case: Converting wide ERP financial forecasts into conformed dimensional tables for Power BI Direct Lake ingestion.

title: Advanced Multi-Branch MERGE INTO with CDC Routing
description: Executing atomic Change Data Capture (CDC) upserts into Delta Lake using multi-branch MERGE INTO statements with conditional updates, hard deletes, soft deletes, and schema evolution.
code:
-- =============================================================================
-- Full CDC Processing: Reconcile Source Binlog into Target Lakehouse
-- =============================================================================
MERGE INTO prod_catalog.silver.customer_master AS target
USING (
    -- Pre-deduplicate incoming CDC micro-batch by record timestamp
    SELECT * FROM (
        SELECT *,
               ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY cdc_timestamp DESC) as rank
        FROM prod_catalog.staging.customer_cdc_stream
    )
    WHERE rank = 1
) AS source
ON target.customer_id = source.customer_id

-- Branch 1: Hard Delete when CDC operation is 'D'
WHEN MATCHED AND source.op_type = 'D' THEN
  DELETE

-- Branch 2: Conditional Update when source is newer than target
WHEN MATCHED AND source.cdc_timestamp > target.updated_at THEN
  UPDATE SET
    target.full_name = source.full_name,
    target.email = source.email,
    target.risk_rating = source.risk_rating,
    target.is_active = source.is_active,
    target.updated_at = source.cdc_timestamp

-- Branch 3: Insert new record when not existing and not deleted
WHEN NOT MATCHED AND source.op_type != 'D' THEN
  INSERT (
    customer_id,
    full_name,
    email,
    risk_rating,
    is_active,
    created_at,
    updated_at
  )
  VALUES (
    source.customer_id,
    source.full_name,
    source.email,
    source.risk_rating,
    true,
    source.cdc_timestamp,
    source.cdc_timestamp
  );
notes: Pre-deduplicating the source batch with ROW_NUMBER() prevents 'Cannot merge because multiple source rows matched the same target row' errors.
Delta Lake MERGE executes atomically with ACID guarantees under Optimistic Concurrency Control.
Adding target.date = source.date in the ON clause triggers partition pruning, skipping 95% of Parquet data scans.
Enable schema evolution by setting spark.databricks.delta.schema.autoMerge.enabled = true.
use_case: Processing Debezium or Oracle GoldenGate CDC streams directly into Silver dimension tables, applying inserts, updates, and deletes in a single atomic commit.

title: Delta Lake Time Travel, Commit Auditing & RESTORE
description: Querying historical versions of Delta tables using VERSION AS OF and TIMESTAMP AS OF, inspecting transaction log commit metadata, and executing emergency rollbacks with RESTORE.
code:
-- 1. Inspect transaction log history, commits, and user identities
DESCRIBE HISTORY prod_catalog.silver.sales_transactions;

-- 2. Time Travel Query: Query table state before a corrupt batch commit
SELECT 
    COUNT(*) AS record_count,
    SUM(txn_amount) AS total_volume
FROM prod_catalog.silver.sales_transactions VERSION AS OF 12;

-- 3. Time Travel Query: Query table as of a specific point in time
SELECT * 
FROM prod_catalog.silver.sales_transactions 
TIMESTAMP AS OF '2026-10-21 18:00:00';

-- 4. Calculate diff between current table state and previous version
SELECT 
    curr.customer_id,
    curr.txn_amount - prev.txn_amount AS amount_difference
FROM prod_catalog.silver.sales_transactions curr
INNER JOIN prod_catalog.silver.sales_transactions VERSION AS OF 11 prev
   ON curr.txn_id = prev.txn_id
WHERE curr.txn_amount != prev.txn_amount;

-- 5. Emergency Rollback: Instantaneously revert table to prior valid version
RESTORE TABLE prod_catalog.silver.sales_transactions TO VERSION AS OF 12;
notes: Delta Lake time travel is powered by the sequential JSON files inside the _delta_log directory.
RESTORE TABLE writes a new forward commit to the log that sets table pointers back to the historical snapshot.
Historical versions remain queryable until VACUUM purges Parquet data files older than the retention period (default 7 days).
DESCRIBE HISTORY shows commit metrics: numOutputRows, numTargetRowsUpdated, and isolationLevel.
use_case: Recovering from an errant pipeline run that corrupted critical financial ledger tables, verifying historical metrics and rolling back in under 2 seconds without restoring from cloud backups.

title: FinOps DBU Consumption & Access Auditing via System Tables
description: Querying Databricks Unity Catalog System Tables (system.billing.usage and system.access.audit) to monitor DBU spend, identify idle expensive clusters, and audit sensitive table access.
code:
-- =============================================================================
-- 1. FinOps: Top 10 Most Expensive Clusters by DBU Cost (Last 30 Days)
-- =============================================================================
SELECT 
    usage_metadata.cluster_id,
    usage_metadata.cluster_name,
    sku_name,
    ROUND(SUM(usage_quantity), 2) AS total_dbus_consumed,
    ROUND(SUM(usage_quantity) * 0.40, 2) AS estimated_usd_cost
FROM system.billing.usage
WHERE usage_date >= current_date() - INTERVAL 30 DAYS
  AND usage_metadata.cluster_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY usage_metadata.cluster_id, usage_metadata.cluster_name, sku_name
ORDER BY total_dbus_consumed DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- =============================================================================
-- 2. Compliance Audit: Identify All Queries Reading PII Tables
-- =============================================================================
SELECT 
    event_time,
    user_identity.email,
    service_name,
    action_name,
    request_params.table_full_name,
    response.status_code
FROM system.access.audit
WHERE request_params.table_full_name LIKE '%customer_dim%'
  AND event_time >= current_date() - INTERVAL 7 DAYS
ORDER BY event_time DESC
LIMIT 50;
notes: System tables are serverless, catalog-level analytical views populated automatically by Databricks control plane.
system.billing.usage provides hourly DBU consumption across all compute types (all-purpose, automated, serverless DBSQL).
system.access.audit tracks every query execution, login event, and permission grant across the workspace.
Can be directly connected to Power BI Direct Lake models to build enterprise FinOps cost control dashboards.
use_case: Setting up automated FinOps alerts to detect rogue un-optimized all-purpose clusters running overnight and auditing compliance for GDPR/HIPAA regulated tables.

title: QUALIFY Clause for In-Line Window Filtering
description: Uses the native QUALIFY clause in Spark SQL / Databricks to filter window function rankings without nested CTEs.
code:
-- Deduplicate customer events, retaining only the latest state per customer
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    event_type,
    event_timestamp,
    payload
FROM customer_events
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY customer_id 
    ORDER BY event_timestamp DESC
) = 1;
notes: QUALIFY evaluates after the WINDOW and SELECT clauses, allowing filtering on window functions directly.
Supported natively in Spark SQL 3.4+ and all Databricks Runtime versions.
Catalyst pushes down the rank limit into the physical SortExec operator, avoiding full dataset buffering.
use_case: Silver-layer deduplication in Medallion lakehouse ingestion pipelines.

title: Adaptive Query Execution Skew Join Hint
description: Enforces automatic partition splitting for known skewed join keys using Spark SQL SKEW hints.
code:
-- Explicit SKEW hint targeting customer_id with hot values (0, NULL)
SELECT /*+ SKEW('f', 'customer_id', (0, NULL)) */
    f.order_id,
    f.amount,
    c.customer_name
FROM fact_sales f
INNER JOIN dim_customer c 
    ON f.customer_id = c.customer_id;
notes: Instructs Catalyst to automatically split partitions containing customer_id in (0, NULL) into smaller sub-partitions.
Replicates the corresponding dimension partition to match each sub-partition.
Eliminates 99% task completion stalls without requiring manual key salting code.
use_case: Joining multi-terabyte transactional tables against master dimensions with heavy default/guest keys.

title: Delta Lake SCD Type 2 MERGE INTO Implementation
description: Standard Delta Lake MERGE statement to expire changed records and insert new active versions for historical tracking.
code:
-- Step 1: Stage incoming changes with null surrogate keys for inserts
MERGE INTO dim_customer AS target
USING (
    -- Join updates against target to identify changed records:
    SELECT 
        updates.customer_id AS merge_key,
        updates.*
    FROM staged_customer_updates updates
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        NULL AS merge_key,
        updates.*
    FROM staged_customer_updates updates
    JOIN dim_customer target 
        ON updates.customer_id = target.customer_id
    WHERE target.is_current = 1 
      AND (target.address <> updates.address OR target.email <> updates.email)
) AS source
ON target.customer_id = source.merge_key
-- Step 2: Expire existing active row
WHEN MATCHED AND target.is_current = 1 AND (target.address <> source.address OR target.email <> source.email) THEN
    UPDATE SET target.is_current = 0, target.end_date = CURRENT_DATE()
-- Step 3: Insert new active row
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN
    INSERT (customer_id, name, address, email, start_date, end_date, is_current)
    VALUES (source.customer_id, source.name, source.address, source.email, CURRENT_DATE(), NULL, 1);
notes: Single-pass MERGE executes atomically under Delta Lake ACID guarantees.
Unioning with merge_key = NULL ensures new rows are inserted in the same transaction.
Guarantees that no customer has overlapping active records (is_current = 1).
use_case: Kimball SCD Type 2 historical dimension processing in Databricks and Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse.

title: Forcing Broadcast Hash Joins with BROADCAST Hint
description: Bypasses network shuffle exchange by broadcasting small dimension tables to all cluster worker nodes.
code:
-- Force Broadcast Hash Join on dim_store (<100MB)
SELECT /*+ BROADCAST(s) */
    f.order_id,
    f.amount,
    s.store_name,
    s.region
FROM fact_sales f
INNER JOIN dim_store s 
    ON f.store_id = s.store_id;
notes: The driver collects dim_store and distributes a read-only copy to all executor memory pools.
fact_sales remains entirely in place with ZERO network shuffle or disk spill.
Recommended for dimension tables up to 100MB (autoBroadcastJoinThreshold defaults to 10MB).
use_case: Star-schema fact-to-dimension joins in Spark SQL.

title: Generating Continuous Date Spines via SEQUENCE()
description: Generates a continuous sequence of calendar dates without recursive CTE overhead using native Spark sequence functions.
notes: sequence() generates an array of dates evaluated in parallel by Catalyst.
explode() projects array elements into individual table rows.
Significantly faster than recursive CTEs in distributed engines.
use_case: Financial reporting, cohort retention, and filling zero-activity date gaps in telemetry.

title: #001 Logical Query Execution Order
description: 1. Enforce understanding of the ANSI SQL Logical Execution Pipeline: (1) FROM -> (2) ON -> (3) JOIN -> (4) WHERE -> (5) GROUP BY -> (6) HAVING -> (7) WINDOW -> (8) SELECT -> (9) DISTINCT -> (10) ORDER BY -> (11) LIMIT 2. Build a production-grade multi-stage CTE pipeline that materializes computed billing metrics, calculates cost-of-goods-sold (COGS) allocations, and filters accounts breaching margin thresholds without alias compilation errors.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Production multi-tier CTE pipeline respecting logical execution order
WITH stg_active_invoices AS (
    -- Step 1 & 2: Filter out non-actionable invoices BEFORE downstream joins and grouping
    SELECT 
        inv.invoice_id,
        inv.tenant_id,
        inv.billing_cycle_month,
        t.organization_name,
        t.pricing_tier,
        t.contract_discount_pct
    FROM saas_billing_invoices inv
    INNER JOIN saas_tenants t ON inv.tenant_id = t.tenant_id
    WHERE inv.invoice_status = 'PAID'
),
invoice_waterfall_aggregates AS (
    -- Step 3 & 4: Aggregate line items to invoice grain, computing net revenue and total COGS
    SELECT 
        inv.tenant_id,
        inv.organization_name,
        inv.pricing_tier,
        inv.billing_cycle_month,
        COUNT(l.line_item_id) AS total_line_items,
        SUM(l.raw_units * l.unit_rate_usd) AS gross_billed_usd,
        ROUND(SUM(l.raw_units * l.unit_rate_usd * (1.0 - inv.contract_discount_pct)), 2) AS net_billed_usd,
        ROUND(SUM(l.allocated_infra_cogs_usd), 2) AS total_cogs_usd
    FROM stg_active_invoices inv
    INNER JOIN saas_invoice_lines l ON inv.invoice_id = l.invoice_id
    GROUP BY 
        inv.tenant_id,
        inv.organization_name,
        inv.pricing_tier,
        inv.billing_cycle_month,
        inv.contract_discount_pct
),
margin_evaluation AS (
    -- Step 5: Project calculated margin expressions in a materialized CTE layer
    -- This resolves aliases so downstream steps can safely filter and sort without 
    -- violating ANSI SQL logical evaluation order!
    SELECT 
        tenant_id,
        organization_name,
        pricing_tier,
        billing_cycle_month,
        gross_billed_usd,
        net_billed_usd,
        total_cogs_usd,
        ROUND(net_billed_usd - total_cogs_usd, 2) AS gross_margin_usd,
        ROUND((net_billed_usd - total_cogs_usd) / NULLIF(net_billed_usd, 0.0), 4) AS effective_margin_pct
    FROM invoice_waterfall_aggregates
)
-- Step 6: Final presentation & audit threshold filtering
SELECT 
    tenant_id,
    organization_name,
    pricing_tier,
    billing_cycle_month,
    net_billed_usd,
    total_cogs_usd,
    gross_margin_usd,
    effective_margin_pct,
    CASE 
        WHEN effective_margin_pct >= 0.50 THEN 'HEALTHY_EXPANSION'
        WHEN effective_margin_pct >= 0.35 THEN 'STABLE_STANDARD'
        ELSE 'CRITICAL_MARGIN_EROSION'
    END AS financial_health_grade
FROM margin_evaluation
WHERE billing_cycle_month = '2024-05'
ORDER BY effective_margin_pct ASC, net_billed_usd DESC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 3
-- ASSERT: COL[tenant_id] = TNT-1002
notes: Engines: PostgreSQL, DuckDB, SQLite, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks Spark SQL
Module: Core SQL Fundamentals
Source: sql-handbook/exercises/01_core_sql_fundamentals/001_logical_query_execution_order.sql
use_case: Enterprise Multi-Tenant SaaS Billing & Margin Reconciliation Engine. Incoming billing transactions stream from Stripe webhooks and ERP feeds into a staging lakehouse layer. Upstream pipeline failures occur when downstream analytical marts attempt non-SARGable predicate filtering on computed projections.

title: #002 Three Valued Logic And Null Traps
description: 1. Illustrate ANSI SQL 3VL truth tables: TRUE, FALSE, and UNKNOWN. 2. Demonstrate how 'column != ''VALUE''' evaluates to UNKNOWN when column IS NULL, which is discarded by the WHERE clause filter. 3. Demonstrate the catastrophic 'NOT IN (subquery with NULL)' collapse bug. 4. Build a production-grade consent evaluation pipeline that handles jurisdiction-specific NULL defaults safely using COALESCE, CASE, and NOT EXISTS.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
WITH stg_customer_consents AS (
    -- Step 1: Left join to capture customers who have no email consent record at all
    SELECT 
        p.customer_id,
        p.full_name,
        p.jurisdiction_code,
        p.primary_email,
        c.consent_status AS raw_consent_status
    FROM customer_privacy_profiles p
    LEFT JOIN marketing_consent_log c 
        ON p.customer_id = c.customer_id 
        AND c.channel = 'EMAIL'
),
evaluated_compliance AS (
    -- Step 2: Apply Three-Valued Logic safely using explicit jurisdiction policies
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        full_name,
        jurisdiction_code,
        primary_email,
        COALESCE(raw_consent_status, 'UNRECORDED_NULL') AS audit_consent_status,
        CASE 
            -- Rule 1: Explicit OPT_OUT is universally disqualified across all legal domains
            WHEN raw_consent_status = 'OPT_OUT' THEN 'EXCLUDED_OPT_OUT'
            
            -- Rule 2: EU GDPR mandates explicit affirmative consent; NULL is non-compliant
            WHEN jurisdiction_code = 'EU_GDPR' AND raw_consent_status = 'OPT_IN' THEN 'ELIGIBLE_GDPR_AFFIRMATIVE'
            WHEN jurisdiction_code = 'EU_GDPR' THEN 'EXCLUDED_GDPR_NO_CONSENT'
            
            -- Rule 3: US CAN-SPAM and APAC permit contact unless explicitly opted out
            WHEN jurisdiction_code IN ('US_CANSPAM', 'APAC') AND (raw_consent_status = 'OPT_IN' OR raw_consent_status IS NULL) 
                THEN 'ELIGIBLE_PERMISSIVE_DEFAULT'
                
            ELSE 'EXCLUDED_UNKNOWN_POLICY'
        END AS compliance_determination
    FROM stg_customer_consents
)
-- Step 3: Dispatch manifest generation selecting strictly legally dispatchable profiles
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    full_name,
    jurisdiction_code,
    primary_email,
    audit_consent_status,
    compliance_determination
FROM evaluated_compliance
WHERE compliance_determination LIKE 'ELIGIBLE%'
ORDER BY jurisdiction_code ASC, customer_id ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 5
-- ASSERT: COL[customer_id] = CUST-005
notes: Engines: PostgreSQL, DuckDB, SQLite, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks Spark SQL

-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Multi-tier security audit report reconciling active organizations, workspace allocations,

WITH org_summary AS (

        o.org_id,
        o.org_slug,
        o.account_status,

title: #005 Safe Type Casting And Numeric Precision
description: Build a data sanitization and high-precision settlement pipeline that cleans raw payload strings, calculates basis point transaction fees, converts to integer cents, and verifies zero-drift balance sheet balancing.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
WITH cleaned_feed AS (
    -- Step 1: Strip non-numeric currency artifacts ('$', 'EUR', 'GBP', ',', whitespace)
    SELECT 
        txn_ref_id,
        currency_code,
        counterparty_id,
        fee_basis_points,
        raw_amount_str,
        -- Clean string: remove commas, currency symbols, and text
        REPLACE(
            REPLACE(
                REPLACE(
                    REPLACE(
                        REPLACE(raw_amount_str, '$', ''), 
                    ',', ''), 
                'EUR', ''), 
            'GBP', ''), 
        ' ', '') AS sanitized_amount_str
    FROM raw_settlement_feed
),
validated_feed AS (
    -- Step 2: Validate numeric conformity; filter out corrupted payload strings
    SELECT 
        txn_ref_id,
        currency_code,
        counterparty_id,
        fee_basis_points,
        -- Check if string represents a valid decimal number
        CASE 
            WHEN sanitized_amount_str GLOB '*[0-9]*' AND NOT sanitized_amount_str GLOB '*[^0-9.]*' 
                THEN CAST(sanitized_amount_str AS DECIMAL(14, 2))
            ELSE NULL 
        END AS clean_amount_local
    FROM cleaned_feed
),
settlement_calculations AS (
    -- Step 3: Perform exact currency conversion and fee deduction in integer cents (preventing float drift)
    SELECT 
        v.txn_ref_id,
        v.counterparty_id,
        v.currency_code,
        v.clean_amount_local,
        r.fx_rate_to_usd,
        -- Calculate gross amount in USD cents
        ROUND(v.clean_amount_local * r.fx_rate_to_usd * 100, 0) AS gross_amount_usd_cents,
        -- Fee calculation: basis points (1 bp = 0.0001)
        ROUND((v.clean_amount_local * r.fx_rate_to_usd * 100) * (v.fee_basis_points / 10000.0), 0) AS fee_usd_cents
    FROM validated_feed v
    INNER JOIN currency_exchange_rates r ON v.currency_code = r.currency_code
    WHERE v.clean_amount_local IS NOT NULL -- Exclude quarantined corrupt payloads
)
-- Step 4: Final project presenting net settlement in USD with high-precision reconciliation
SELECT 
    txn_ref_id,
    counterparty_id,
    currency_code,
    clean_amount_local,
    fx_rate_to_usd,
    CAST(gross_amount_usd_cents / 100.0 AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) AS gross_usd,
    CAST(fee_usd_cents / 100.0 AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) AS fee_usd,
    CAST((gross_amount_usd_cents - fee_usd_cents) / 100.0 AS DECIMAL(12, 2)) AS net_settlement_usd
FROM settlement_calculations
ORDER BY gross_amount_usd_cents DESC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 6
-- ASSERT: COL[txn_ref_id] = TXN-8803

title: #006 String Manipulation And Pattern Extraction
description: Parse the raw log payload using standard ANSI SQL string manipulation functions: INSTR, SUBSTR, LENGTH, REPLACE, and TRIM. Generate an enterprise SIEM audit manifest.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
WITH tokenized_logs AS (
    SELECT 
        log_id,
        raw_payload,
        -- Extract Client IP: substring from start to first space
        SUBSTR(raw_payload, 1, INSTR(raw_payload, ' ') - 1) AS client_ip,
        -- Extract Email: substring between '- ' and ' ['
        SUBSTR(
            raw_payload,
            INSTR(raw_payload, '- ') + 2,
            INSTR(raw_payload, ' [') - (INSTR(raw_payload, '- ') + 2)
        ) AS raw_email,
        -- Extract Request Line: substring between first quote '"' and second quote '"'
        SUBSTR(
            raw_payload,
            INSTR(raw_payload, '"') + 1,
            INSTR(SUBSTR(raw_payload, INSTR(raw_payload, '"') + 1), '"') - 1
        ) AS request_line,
        -- Extract Status Code: last 7 characters before response size (e.g. ' 200 4520')
        CAST(SUBSTR(raw_payload, INSTR(raw_payload, '" ') + 2, 3) AS INT) AS http_status
    FROM raw_siem_ingress_logs
),
parsed_fields AS (
    SELECT 
        log_id,
        client_ip,
        raw_email,
        -- HTTP Method: token before first space in request_line
        SUBSTR(request_line, 1, INSTR(request_line, ' ') - 1) AS http_method,
        -- URI Path: token between first space and last space in request_line
        SUBSTR(
            request_line,
            INSTR(request_line, ' ') + 1,
            INSTR(SUBSTR(request_line, INSTR(request_line, ' ') + 1), ' ') - 1
        ) AS uri_path,
        http_status
    FROM tokenized_logs
),
masked_compliance_layer AS (
    SELECT 
        log_id,
        -- Pseudonymize IP to /24 Class C subnet: keep first 3 octets, mask 4th octet
        SUBSTR(client_ip, 1, INSTR(client_ip, '.') - 1) || '.0.0.0/8' AS anonymized_subnet,
        -- Email domain extraction
        SUBSTR(raw_email, INSTR(raw_email, '@') + 1) AS email_domain,
        -- PII Masking: first char + '***' + '@domain'
        SUBSTR(raw_email, 1, 1) || '***@' || SUBSTR(raw_email, INSTR(raw_email, '@') + 1) AS masked_email,
        http_method,
        uri_path,
        http_status
    FROM parsed_fields
)
SELECT 
    log_id,
    anonymized_subnet,
    masked_email,
    http_method,
    uri_path,
    http_status,
    CASE 
        WHEN http_status >= 500 THEN 'SEV1_SERVER_ERROR'
        WHEN http_status = 404 THEN 'WARN_NOT_FOUND'
        WHEN http_method IN ('POST', 'DELETE') THEN 'AUDIT_STATE_MUTATION'
        ELSE 'INFO_READ_TRAFFIC'
    END AS telemetry_classification
FROM masked_compliance_layer
ORDER BY log_id ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 6
-- ASSERT: COL[log_id] = LOG-001

title: #007 Temporal And Timestamp Arithmetic
description: Build a temporal analytics pipeline that converts ISO timestamps into Julian day offsets, calculates total turnaround hours, isolates transit vs customs delay hours, and determines SLA compliance flags.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
WITH temporal_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        consignment_id,
        origin_hub,
        destination_hub,
        dispatched_at,
        delivered_at,
        contracted_sla_hours,
        -- Calculate total elapsed hours using Julian day differences multiplied by 24.0 hours/day
        ROUND((JULIANDAY(delivered_at) - JULIANDAY(dispatched_at)) * 24.0, 2) AS total_elapsed_hours,
        -- Calculate customs hold duration if applicable
        CASE 
            WHEN customs_released_at IS NOT NULL 
                THEN ROUND((JULIANDAY(customs_released_at) - JULIANDAY(dispatched_at)) * 24.0, 2)
            ELSE 0.00
        END AS customs_processing_hours
    FROM freight_consignments
),
sla_evaluation AS (
    SELECT 
        consignment_id,
        origin_hub,
        destination_hub,
        contracted_sla_hours,
        total_elapsed_hours,
        customs_processing_hours,
        -- Net active transit hours excluding customs hold
        ROUND(total_elapsed_hours - (customs_processing_hours * 0.5), 2) AS billable_transit_hours,
        CASE 
            WHEN total_elapsed_hours <= contracted_sla_hours THEN 'SLA_MET_ON_TIME'
            WHEN total_elapsed_hours <= (contracted_sla_hours + 4) THEN 'SLA_GRACE_PERIOD'
            ELSE 'SLA_BREACH_PENALTY'
        END AS delivery_performance_tier
    FROM temporal_metrics
)
SELECT 
    consignment_id,
    origin_hub,
    destination_hub,
    contracted_sla_hours,
    total_elapsed_hours,
    billable_transit_hours,
    delivery_performance_tier
FROM sla_evaluation
ORDER BY total_elapsed_hours DESC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 5
-- ASSERT: COL[consignment_id] = PKG-1003

title: #008 Conditional Case Logic And Nullif Coalesce
description: Construct a multi-branch CASE expression pipeline that safely evaluates promotional discounts, guards against division by zero via NULLIF, and computes net settled revenue.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
WITH tiered_discounts AS (
    SELECT 
        order_id,
        customer_tier,
        product_category,
        gross_merchandise_value,
        ordered_units,
        returned_units,
        -- Tier 1 Loyalty Discount rate
        CASE 
            WHEN customer_tier = 'VIP_PLATINUM' THEN 0.20
            WHEN customer_tier = 'VIP_GOLD' THEN 0.10
            ELSE 0.00
        END AS loyalty_discount_rate,
        -- Coupon fixed discount
        CASE 
            WHEN coupon_code = 'SPRING10' THEN 0.10
            WHEN coupon_code = 'FLAT20' THEN 0.00 -- handled as flat deduction
            WHEN coupon_code = 'VIPCLEAR' THEN 0.15
            ELSE 0.00
        END AS coupon_pct_rate,
        CASE WHEN coupon_code = 'FLAT20' THEN 20.00 ELSE 0.00 END AS coupon_flat_usd
    FROM d2c_order_settlements
),
financial_waterfall AS (
    SELECT 
        order_id,
        customer_tier,
        product_category,
        gross_merchandise_value,
        ordered_units,
        returned_units,
        -- Safe return rate calculation guarding against DIVISION BY ZERO via NULLIF
        ROUND(CAST(returned_units AS DECIMAL) / NULLIF(ordered_units, 0), 4) AS return_ratio,
        -- Net value after loyalty discount and coupon
        ROUND(
            (gross_merchandise_value * (1.0 - loyalty_discount_rate) * (1.0 - coupon_pct_rate)) - coupon_flat_usd, 
            2
        ) AS discounted_order_value,
        -- Return restocking fee calculation
        CASE 
            WHEN returned_units = 0 THEN 0.00
            WHEN product_category = 'ELECTRONICS' THEN ROUND(gross_merchandise_value * 0.15, 2)
            WHEN product_category = 'APPAREL' THEN 0.00
            ELSE 5.00
        END AS restocking_fee_usd
    FROM tiered_discounts
)
SELECT 
    order_id,
    customer_tier,
    product_category,
    gross_merchandise_value,
    COALESCE(return_ratio, 0.0000) AS clean_return_ratio,
    discounted_order_value,
    restocking_fee_usd,
    ROUND(discounted_order_value + restocking_fee_usd, 2) AS final_net_settled_revenue
FROM financial_waterfall
ORDER BY final_net_settled_revenue DESC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 6
-- ASSERT: COL[order_id] = ORD-501

title: #011 Inner Left Right Full Outer Joins
description: Construct a robust revenue attribution query that correctly demonstrates the semantic difference between filtering in the ON clause vs WHERE clause of an outer join, producing an enterprise sales leaderboard with zero data loss.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Correct pattern: Condition 'deal_stage = CLOSED_WON' placed inside ON clause
-- to preserve all representatives on the left side of the relation!
WITH rep_deal_aggregates AS (
    SELECT 
        r.rep_id,
        r.rep_name,
        r.territory,
        r.quarterly_quota_usd,
        COUNT(d.deal_id) AS total_won_deals_count,
        COALESCE(SUM(d.deal_amount_usd), 0.00) AS total_won_revenue_usd
    FROM sales_reps r
    LEFT JOIN sales_deals d 
        ON r.rep_id = d.rep_id 
        AND d.deal_stage = 'CLOSED_WON' -- Crucial: Evaluated during join pass!
    GROUP BY 
        r.rep_id, 
        r.rep_name, 
        r.territory, 
        r.quarterly_quota_usd
),
quota_attainment_scoring AS (
    SELECT 
        rep_id,
        rep_name,
        territory,
        quarterly_quota_usd,
        total_won_deals_count,
        total_won_revenue_usd,
        ROUND((total_won_revenue_usd / NULLIF(quarterly_quota_usd, 0.00)) * 100.0, 2) AS quota_attainment_pct
    FROM rep_deal_aggregates
)
SELECT 
    rep_id,
    rep_name,
    territory,
    quarterly_quota_usd,
    total_won_deals_count,
    total_won_revenue_usd,
    quota_attainment_pct,
    CASE 
        WHEN quota_attainment_pct >= 100.0 THEN 'QUOTA_ACHIEVED_BONUS'
        WHEN quota_attainment_pct >= 70.0  THEN 'ON_TRACK'
        WHEN total_won_revenue_usd = 0.00 THEN 'ZERO_WON_DEALS_ATTENTION'
        ELSE 'BELOW_QUOTA_COACHING'
    END AS performance_bracket
FROM quota_attainment_scoring
ORDER BY total_won_revenue_usd DESC, rep_id ASC;

-- ASSERT: COL[rep_id] = REP-101

        bk.cleared_amount_usd AS bk_amount

),
right_orphans AS (

        bk.reference_id AS bk_ref,

        bk.cleared_amount_usd AS bk_amount
    FROM external_bank_feed bk
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM internal_gl_entries gl WHERE gl.reference_id = bk.reference_id
    )
),
full_recon_matrix AS (
    SELECT * FROM left_side
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM right_orphans
)
SELECT 
    COALESCE(gl_ref, bk_ref) AS reconciled_reference_id,
    gl_amount,
    bk_amount,
    ROUND(COALESCE(gl_amount, 0.00) - COALESCE(bk_amount, 0.00), 2) AS variance_usd,
    CASE 
        WHEN gl_ref IS NOT NULL AND bk_ref IS NOT NULL AND gl_amount = bk_amount THEN 'RECONCILED_MATCH'
        WHEN gl_ref IS NOT NULL AND bk_ref IS NOT NULL AND gl_amount != bk_amount THEN 'AMOUNT_MISMATCH_DISPUTE'
        WHEN gl_ref IS NOT NULL AND bk_ref IS NULL THEN 'LEDGER_ONLY_UNCLEARED'
        WHEN gl_ref IS NULL AND bk_ref IS NOT NULL THEN 'BANK_ONLY_UNRECORDED_FEE'
    END AS reconciliation_status
FROM full_recon_matrix
ORDER BY reconciled_reference_id ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 5
-- ASSERT: COL[reconciled_reference_id] = REF-100

title: #015 Cross Joins And Cartesian Grid Generation

-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Production dense grid generation:
-- 1. CROSS JOIN store × product × date generates 18 theoretical combinations
-- 2. LEFT JOIN against sparse sales imputes 0 for non-active sales days
WITH dense_scaffold AS (
    SELECT 
        s.store_id,
        s.store_name,
        p.sku_id,
        p.product_name,
        d.date_key AS reporting_date
    FROM dim_stores s
    CROSS JOIN dim_products p
    CROSS JOIN dim_dates d
)
SELECT 
    grid.reporting_date,
    grid.store_id,
    grid.store_name,
    grid.sku_id,
    grid.product_name,
    COALESCE(pos.units_sold, 0) AS units_sold,
    COALESCE(pos.revenue_usd, 0.00) AS revenue_usd,
    CASE WHEN pos.units_sold IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_imputed_zero
FROM dense_scaffold grid
LEFT JOIN actual_pos_sales pos 
    ON grid.store_id = pos.store_id 
    AND grid.sku_id = pos.sku_id 
    AND grid.reporting_date = pos.sale_date
ORDER BY grid.reporting_date ASC, grid.store_id ASC, grid.sku_id ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---

-- ASSERT: COL[store_id] = STR-01

SELECT

    t.currency_pair,

-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Standard ANSI SQL correlated ranking: Extracts Top-2 highest-value transactions per client
WITH ranked_client_txns AS (

        c.client_id,
        c.client_name,
        c.industry_tier,
        t.txn_id,

            PARTITION BY c.client_id

    txn_id,
    txn_amount_usd,

title: #018 Union Vs Union All Internals
description: Consolidate disparate ingestion channels using UNION ALL while calculating channel contributions, and demonstrate the exact duplicate identification audit.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- High-throughput streaming consolidation:
-- 1. UNION ALL provides zero-overhead concatenation
-- 2. Audit metadata tags the source channel
-- 3. Downstream windowing flags duplicate events deterministically
WITH unified_stream AS (
    SELECT event_id, user_id, action_type, event_timestamp, 'WEB_CHANNEL' AS ingestion_source
    FROM web_click_stream
    
    UNION ALL
    
    SELECT event_id, user_id, action_type, event_timestamp, 'MOBILE_CHANNEL' AS ingestion_source
    FROM mobile_app_stream
),
dedup_audited AS (
    SELECT 
        event_id,
        user_id,
        action_type,
        event_timestamp,
        ingestion_source,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY event_id 
            ORDER BY ingestion_source ASC
        ) AS occurrence_rank
    FROM unified_stream
)
SELECT 
    event_id,
    user_id,
    action_type,
    event_timestamp,
    ingestion_source,
    CASE 
        WHEN occurrence_rank = 1 THEN 'PRIMARY_DELIVERY'
        ELSE 'DUPLICATE_CROSS_CHANNEL_REPLAY'
    END AS stream_delivery_status
FROM dedup_audited
ORDER BY event_timestamp ASC, event_id ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 6
-- ASSERT: COL[event_id] = EV-W1

title: #020 Self Joins For Sequential Event Pairs
description: Build a self-join event pair pipeline that links each user action to its immediate subsequent action, calculates transition elapsed seconds, and flags drop-offs.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Self-join pattern linking step_sequence N to step_sequence N + 1
SELECT 
    curr.session_id,
    curr.step_sequence AS from_step_num,
    curr.page_name AS from_page,
    nxt.step_sequence AS to_step_num,
    COALESCE(nxt.page_name, 'SESSION_ABANDONED_EXIT') AS to_page,
    CASE 
        WHEN nxt.event_epoch_sec IS NOT NULL THEN (nxt.event_epoch_sec - curr.event_epoch_sec)
        ELSE NULL 
    END AS transition_duration_seconds,
    CASE 
        WHEN nxt.page_name IS NULL THEN 'CHURN_DROP_OFF'
        WHEN (nxt.event_epoch_sec - curr.event_epoch_sec) > 90 THEN 'SLOW_FRICTION_TRANSITION'
        ELSE 'OPTIMAL_VELOCITY'
    END AS transition_health_grade
FROM user_clickstream_events curr
LEFT JOIN user_clickstream_events nxt 
    ON curr.session_id = nxt.session_id 
    AND curr.step_sequence + 1 = nxt.step_sequence
ORDER BY curr.session_id ASC, curr.step_sequence ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 7
-- ASSERT: COL[session_id] = S1

-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Single-pass conditional aggregation SaaS ARR waterfall
SELECT 
    cohort_month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS total_active_movement_accounts,
    -- Conditional sums calculating ARR components
    SUM(CASE WHEN movement_type = 'NEW_ARR' THEN delta_mrr_usd ELSE 0.00 END) AS new_arr_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN movement_type = 'EXPANSION' THEN delta_mrr_usd ELSE 0.00 END) AS expansion_arr_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN movement_type = 'CONTRACTION' THEN delta_mrr_usd ELSE 0.00 END) AS contraction_arr_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN movement_type = 'CHURN' THEN delta_mrr_usd ELSE 0.00 END) AS churned_arr_usd,
    -- Net New ARR calculation
    SUM(delta_mrr_usd) AS net_new_arr_usd,
    -- Percentage of positive growth derived from existing account expansion
    ROUND(
        SUM(CASE WHEN movement_type = 'EXPANSION' THEN delta_mrr_usd ELSE 0.00 END) / 
        NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN movement_type IN ('NEW_ARR', 'EXPANSION') THEN delta_mrr_usd ELSE 0.00 END), 0) * 100.0, 
        2
    ) AS expansion_growth_share_pct
FROM saas_subscription_movements
GROUP BY cohort_month
ORDER BY cohort_month ASC;

title: #025 Multidimensional OLAP Rollup Subtotals
description: Produce a hierarchical sales rollup report displaying store details, regional subtotals, and global totals with clean presentation labels.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Hierarchical ROLLUP emulation:
-- Level 1: [Region, Country, Store] (Detailed Grain)
-- Level 2: [Region, Country, ALL]   (Country Subtotal)
-- Level 3: [Region, ALL, ALL]       (Region Subtotal)
-- Level 4: [ALL, ALL, ALL]          (Grand Global Total)
WITH detailed_leaf AS (
    SELECT region, country, store_name, SUM(total_sales_usd) AS sales_usd, 1 AS hierarchy_level
    FROM store_sales_summary
    GROUP BY region, country, store_name
),
country_subtotals AS (
    SELECT region, country, '--- ALL STORES ---' AS store_name, SUM(total_sales_usd) AS sales_usd, 2 AS hierarchy_level
    FROM store_sales_summary
    GROUP BY region, country
),
region_subtotals AS (
    SELECT region, '--- ALL COUNTRIES ---' AS country, '--- ALL STORES ---' AS store_name, SUM(total_sales_usd) AS sales_usd, 3 AS hierarchy_level
    FROM store_sales_summary
    GROUP BY region
),
grand_total AS (
    SELECT '--- GLOBAL TOTAL ---' AS region, '--- ALL COUNTRIES ---' AS country, '--- ALL STORES ---' AS store_name, SUM(total_sales_usd) AS sales_usd, 4 AS hierarchy_level
    FROM store_sales_summary
)
SELECT region, country, store_name, sales_usd, hierarchy_level
FROM (
    SELECT * FROM detailed_leaf
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM country_subtotals
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM region_subtotals
    UNION ALL
    SELECT * FROM grand_total
)
ORDER BY 
    CASE WHEN region LIKE '---%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END ASC,
    region ASC,
    CASE WHEN country LIKE '---%' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END ASC,
    country ASC,
    hierarchy_level ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 13
-- ASSERT: COL[region] = AMER

title: #028 Relational Pivoting Rows To Columns
description: Implement an enterprise-grade query to resolve 028 relational pivoting rows to columns.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Universal ANSI SQL Pivot transforming quarterly rows into columnar balance sheet
SELECT 
    cost_center,
    SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_quarter = '2024-Q1' THEN spend_amount_usd ELSE 0.00 END) AS q1_actual_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_quarter = '2024-Q2' THEN spend_amount_usd ELSE 0.00 END) AS q2_actual_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_quarter = '2024-Q3' THEN spend_amount_usd ELSE 0.00 END) AS q3_actual_usd,
    SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_quarter = '2024-Q4' THEN spend_amount_usd ELSE 0.00 END) AS q4_actual_usd,
    SUM(spend_amount_usd) AS full_year_total_usd,
    ROUND(
        (SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_quarter = '2024-Q4' THEN spend_amount_usd ELSE 0.00 END) - 
         SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_quarter = '2024-Q1' THEN spend_amount_usd ELSE 0.00 END)) / 
        NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN fiscal_quarter = '2024-Q1' THEN spend_amount_usd ELSE 0.00 END), 0.00) * 100.0, 
        2
    ) AS full_year_spend_growth_pct
FROM accounting_gl_summary
GROUP BY cost_center
ORDER BY full_year_total_usd DESC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---

-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Exact continuous percentile calculation using NTILE bucketing and window ranking
WITH ranked_requests AS (
    SELECT 
        endpoint_name,
        latency_ms,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY endpoint_name ORDER BY latency_ms ASC) AS rank_idx,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY endpoint_name) AS total_requests
    FROM api_request_telemetry

FROM ranked_requests

-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
WITH lagged_events AS (
    SELECT 
        event_id,
        user_id,
        event_timestamp,
        epoch_sec,
        page_url,
        LAG(epoch_sec) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY epoch_sec ASC) AS prev_epoch_sec
    FROM user_raw_events
),
session_boundaries AS (
    SELECT 
        event_id,
        user_id,
        event_timestamp,
        epoch_sec,
        page_url,
        -- Flag new session if gap > 1800 seconds (30 minutes) or first event
        CASE 
            WHEN prev_epoch_sec IS NULL OR (epoch_sec - prev_epoch_sec) > 1800 THEN 1 
            ELSE 0 
        END AS is_new_session_flag
    FROM lagged_events
),
assigned_sessions AS (
    SELECT 
        event_id,
        user_id,
        event_timestamp,
        page_url,
        -- Running sum creates unique session index per user
        SUM(is_new_session_flag) OVER (
            PARTITION BY user_id 
            ORDER BY epoch_sec ASC 
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS session_seq_num
    FROM session_boundaries
)
SELECT 
    user_id,
    session_seq_num,
    COUNT(event_id) AS total_events_in_session,
    MIN(event_timestamp) AS session_started_at,
    MAX(event_timestamp) AS session_ended_at

description: Write a production-grade SQL query fulfilling the architectural requirements for 040 gaps and islands overlapping interval merging.

-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Merging overlapping intervals:
-- 1. Identify previous max end_time using window MAX()
-- 2. Detect boundary break when current start_time > prev max end_time
WITH max_previous_interval AS (
    SELECT 
        cluster_id,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        MAX(end_time) OVER (
            PARTITION BY cluster_id 
            ORDER BY start_time ASC 
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND 1 PRECEDING
        ) AS max_prev_end_time
    FROM container_lease_intervals
),
interval_groups AS (
    SELECT 
        cluster_id,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        -- New group starts if current start is past previous max end
        CASE 
            WHEN max_prev_end_time IS NULL OR start_time > max_prev_end_time THEN 1 
            ELSE 0 
        END AS is_new_block_flag
    FROM max_previous_interval
),
clustered_blocks AS (
    SELECT 
        cluster_id,
        start_time,
        end_time,
        SUM(is_new_block_flag) OVER (
            PARTITION BY cluster_id 
            ORDER BY start_time ASC
            ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS block_id
    FROM interval_groups
)
SELECT 
    cluster_id,
    block_id,
    MIN(start_time) AS merged_active_start,
    MAX(end_time)   AS merged_active_end,
    ROUND((JULIANDAY(MAX(end_time)) - JULIANDAY(MIN(start_time))) * 24.0, 2) AS billable_duration_hours
FROM clustered_blocks
GROUP BY cluster_id, block_id
ORDER BY merged_active_start ASC;

        COUNT(DISTINCT a.customer_id) AS active_users
    FROM customer_signups s
    INNER JOIN customer_monthly_activity a ON s.customer_id = a.customer_id
    GROUP BY s.signup_month, a.active_month
)
SELECT 
    a.signup_month,
    c.cohort_initial_users,
    a.month_number,
    a.active_users,
    ROUND((CAST(a.active_users AS DECIMAL) / c.cohort_initial_users) * 100.0, 2) AS retention_rate_pct
FROM active_by_cohort a
INNER JOIN cohort_sizes c ON a.signup_month = c.signup_month
ORDER BY a.signup_month ASC, a.month_number ASC;

    -- Anchor Member: Start at the root of the hierarchy (CEO)

        emp_name,

        manager_id,

)

-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Recursive path traversal with cycle prevention via path string inspection
WITH RECURSIVE flight_paths AS (
    -- Anchor: Direct departures from JFK
    SELECT 
        origin,
        destination,
        cost_usd AS total_cost_usd,
        1 AS flight_hops,
        origin || '->' || destination AS flight_itinerary
    FROM flight_routes
    WHERE origin = 'JFK'
    
    UNION ALL
    
    -- Recursive: Extend path while ensuring next destination is NOT already in itinerary (Cycle Prevention)
    SELECT 
        parent.origin,
        nxt.destination,
        ROUND(parent.total_cost_usd + nxt.cost_usd, 2) AS total_cost_usd,
        parent.flight_hops + 1 AS flight_hops,
        parent.flight_itinerary || '->' || nxt.destination AS flight_itinerary
    FROM flight_routes nxt
    INNER JOIN flight_paths parent ON nxt.origin = parent.destination
    WHERE parent.flight_itinerary NOT LIKE '%' || nxt.destination || '%'
      AND parent.flight_hops < 4 -- Guardrail max hops
)
SELECT 
    origin,
    destination,
    flight_hops,
    total_cost_usd,
    flight_itinerary
FROM flight_paths
WHERE destination = 'LHR'
ORDER BY total_cost_usd ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---

title: #078 Non Repeatable Read Anomaly
description: Model a temporal snapshot inventory ledger tracking warehouse SKU stock across snapshot points (T1 = 10:00:00 and T2 = 10:05:00). Write an analytical query demonstrating how a Repeatable Read snapshot freezes the point-in-time value at T1 (100 units) regardless of subsequent committed deductions.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Simulates REPEATABLE READ snapshot consistency at T1 ('2024-06-01 10:00:00')
-- vs READ COMMITTED view at current time ('2024-06-01 10:05:00')
WITH snapshot_t1_view AS (
    SELECT 
        i.sku_id,
        i.warehouse_id,
        i.base_stock_units + COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN m.committed_at <= '2024-06-01 10:00:00' THEN m.delta_units ELSE 0 END), 0) AS stock_at_repeatable_read_t1
    FROM warehouse_sku_inventory i
    LEFT JOIN inventory_mutation_log m ON i.sku_id = m.sku_id
    GROUP BY i.sku_id, i.warehouse_id, i.base_stock_units
),
current_committed_view AS (
    SELECT 
        i.sku_id,
        i.base_stock_units + COALESCE(SUM(m.delta_units), 0) AS stock_at_read_committed_t2
    FROM warehouse_sku_inventory i
    LEFT JOIN inventory_mutation_log m ON i.sku_id = m.sku_id
    GROUP BY i.sku_id, i.base_stock_units
)
SELECT 
    t1.sku_id,
    t1.warehouse_id,
    t1.stock_at_repeatable_read_t1,
    t2.stock_at_read_committed_t2,
    (t1.stock_at_repeatable_read_t1 - t2.stock_at_read_committed_t2) AS committed_drift_delta,
    'REPEATABLE_READ_PROTECTS_AGAINST_FUZZY_DRIFT' AS concurrency_mechanism
FROM snapshot_t1_view t1
INNER JOIN current_committed_view t2 ON t1.sku_id = t2.sku_id;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 1
-- ASSERT: COL[sku_id] = SKU-GRAPHICS-CARD
-- ASSERT: COL[stock_at_repeatable_read_t1] = 100
-- ASSERT: COL[stock_at_read_committed_t2] = 65
-- ASSERT: COL[committed_drift_delta] = 35\n

use_case: Multi-Tier Inventory Rebalancing & Warehouse Allocation Service. Non-Repeatable Read (Fuzzy Read) Anomaly: - Under READ COMMITTED isolation: Transaction A reads SKU stock at T1 (finds 50 units). - Concurrently, Transaction B issues UPDATE deducting 30 units and commits at T2. - Transaction A re-reads the exact same SKU at T3 within the same transaction and finds 20 units!     FROM commercial_lending_facilities
    WHERE risk_tier = 'TIER_1_CRITICAL'
      AND facility_limit_usd >= 1000000.00
      AND approved_at <= '2024-06-01 10:30:00'
)
SELECT 
    t1.initial_facility_count,
    t1.initial_total_exposure_usd,
    t2.subsequent_facility_count,
    t2.subsequent_total_exposure_usd,
    (t2.subsequent_facility_count - t1.initial_facility_count) AS phantom_row_count,
    (t2.subsequent_total_exposure_usd - t1.initial_total_exposure_usd) AS phantom_exposure_delta_usd,
    'SERIALIZABLE_ISOLATION_REQUIRED_TO_PREVENT_PHANTOMS' AS architecture_remediation
FROM t1_initial_range_scan t1
CROSS JOIN t2_subsequent_range_scan t2;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 1
-- ASSERT: COL[initial_facility_count] = 2
-- ASSERT: COL[subsequent_facility_count] = 3

-- Audit query detecting the write skew anomaly and evaluating active doctor count
WITH on_call_evaluation AS (
    SELECT

        WHEN e.active_on_call_physicians >= 1 THEN 'COMPLIANT_COVERAGE'
    END AS invariant_health_status,
    'ENFORCE_SERIALIZABLE_OR_MUTEX_ROW_LOCK' AS architectural_remedy
FROM on_call_evaluation e;

Write Skew Anomaly: - Invariant: At all times, at least 1 physician must remain on call (COUNT(on_call) >= 1). - Currently on call: Dr. Alice and Dr. Bob (COUNT = 2). - Transaction 1 (Dr. Alice): Checks COUNT(*) WHERE is_on_call = 1. Sees 2. Decides it is safe to take leave and sets Dr. Alice's is_on_call = 0. - Concurrently, Transaction 2 (Dr. Bob): Checks COUNT(*) WHERE is_on_call = 1. Sees 2. Decides it is safe to take leave and sets Dr. Bob's is_on_call = 0. - Under Snapshot Isolation, BOTH transactions commit! Why? They modified disjoint rows! - Result: 0 doctors on call. Severe invariant failure (Write Skew)!

title: #081 MVCC Internals And Version Visibility
description: Model a physical MVCC heap table with tuple versions for customer account ACC-801. Evaluate tuple visibility for an active transaction snapshot at tx_id = 104, and classify which tuples are LIVE_VISIBLE, FUTURE_INVISIBLE, or DEAD_GARBAGE.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Evaluate MVCC visibility for a reader holding Snapshot Tx = 104
SELECT 
    tuple_id,
    account_id,
    balance_usd,
    xmin,
    xmax,
    CASE 
        WHEN xmin <= 104 AND (xmax > 104 OR xmax = 0) THEN 'LIVE_VISIBLE'
        WHEN xmin > 104 THEN 'FUTURE_INVISIBLE'
        WHEN xmin <= 104 AND xmax <= 104 AND xmax != 0 THEN 'DEAD_GARBAGE_TUPLE'
    END AS tuple_visibility_status,
    CASE 
        WHEN xmax != 0 AND xmax <= 104 THEN 'VACUUM_RECLAIMABLE'
        ELSE 'RETAIN'
    END AS vacuum_lifecycle
FROM pg_heap_tuples
ORDER BY tuple_id ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 4
-- ASSERT: COL[tuple_id] = 1
-- ASSERT: COL[tuple_visibility_status] = DEAD_GARBAGE_TUPLE\n
notes: Engines: PostgreSQL, DuckDB, SQLite, Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks Spark SQL
Module: Transactions Concurrency And Locks
Source: sql-handbook/exercises/08_transactions_concurrency_and_locks/081_mvcc_internals_and_version_visibility.sql
use_case: PostgreSQL & Distributed Storage Engine MVCC Internals. In Multi-Version Concurrency Control (MVCC), rows are immutable heap tuples. Each physical tuple header stores: 1. xmin: Transaction ID that inserted/created the tuple. 2. xmax: Transaction ID that deleted or superseded the tuple (0 if currently active/alive). 3. Tuple Visibility Rule for Snapshot at Tx_ID = S: A tuple is VISIBLE if: (xmin <= S AND xmin is committed) AND (xmax > S OR xmax = 0 OR xmax is uncommitted/aborted). When xmax <= S and committed, the tuple is DEAD and eligible for VACUUM cleanup.

title: #083 Deadlock Reproduction And Inverse Locking
description: Model a wire transfer routing engine. Given pending concurrent transfer requests, write a query that computes the canonical lock acquisition sequence for each transfer and verifies that canonical ordering prevents cyclic lock contention.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Determine canonical locking sequence to guarantee deadlock immunity
SELECT 
    t.transfer_id,
    t.source_account_id,
    t.target_account_id,
    t.transfer_amount_usd,
    CASE 
        WHEN t.source_account_id < t.target_account_id THEN t.source_account_id 
        ELSE t.target_account_id 
    END AS primary_lock_resource,
    CASE 
        WHEN t.source_account_id < t.target_account_id THEN t.target_account_id 
        ELSE t.source_account_id 
    END AS secondary_lock_resource,
    'CANONICAL_SORT_PREVENTS_DEADLOCK_CYCLES' AS lock_protocol_strategy
FROM pending_wire_transfers t
ORDER BY t.transfer_id ASC;

-- ASSERT: COL[primary_lock_resource] = ACC-101
-- ASSERT: COL[secondary_lock_resource] = ACC-202\n

title: #085 Double Entry Ledger Atomic Transfer
description: Build a production-grade multi-leg general ledger auditing query that: 1. Reconciles all journal batches and verifies that every batch mathematically balances to 0.00. 2. Evaluates trial balance totals by account class (ASSET, LIABILITY, REVENUE). 3. Flags any corrupted or unbalanced transaction batches.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Master General Ledger batch audit verifying Pacioli Zero-Balance Invariant
WITH batch_balance_check AS (
    SELECT 
        b.batch_id,
        b.batch_reference,
        b.posted_timestamp,
        COUNT(l.line_id) AS total_legs,
        SUM(l.amount_usd) AS net_batch_balance_usd,
        SUM(CASE WHEN l.amount_usd > 0 THEN l.amount_usd ELSE 0 END) AS total_debits_usd,
        SUM(CASE WHEN l.amount_usd < 0 THEN ABS(l.amount_usd) ELSE 0 END) AS total_credits_usd
    FROM gl_journal_batches b
    INNER JOIN gl_journal_lines l ON b.batch_id = l.batch_id
    GROUP BY b.batch_id, b.batch_reference, b.posted_timestamp
)
SELECT 
    batch_id,
    batch_reference,
    total_legs,
    total_debits_usd,
    total_credits_usd,
    net_batch_balance_usd,
    CASE 
        WHEN net_batch_balance_usd = 0.00 THEN 'ZERO_BALANCE_INVARIANT_CONFIRMED'
        ELSE 'CRITICAL_LEDGER_IMBALANCE_DETECTED'
    END AS ledger_audit_status
FROM batch_balance_check
ORDER BY batch_id ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 1
-- ASSERT: COL[batch_id] = BATCH-2024-8801
-- ASSERT: COL[total_legs] = 4
-- ASSERT: COL[net_batch_balance_usd] = 0.0
-- ASSERT: COL[ledger_audit_status] = ZERO_BALANCE_INVARIANT_CONFIRMED\n

title: #086 Snowflake Micropartition Pruning
description: Model a cloud warehouse metadata catalog tracking 4 micro-partitions of an enterprise audit event table. Write a query simulating the metadata pruning optimizer for a target query searching for events on '2024-05-16' in tenant 'TNT-US-CORP'. Calculate partitions scanned vs pruned and row scanning efficiency.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Query optimizer evaluation: targeting '2024-05-16 14:00:00' and 'TNT-US-CORP'
WITH optimizer_pruning_decision AS (
    SELECT 
        partition_id,
        min_event_time,
        max_event_time,
        min_tenant_id,
        max_tenant_id,
        row_count,
        compressed_bytes,
        CASE 
            WHEN '2024-05-16 14:00:00' BETWEEN min_event_time AND max_event_time
             AND 'TNT-US-CORP' BETWEEN min_tenant_id AND max_tenant_id
            THEN 'SCAN_CANDIDATE'
            ELSE 'METADATA_PRUNED'
        END AS pruning_verdict
    FROM micropartition_catalog
)
SELECT 
    COUNT(*) AS total_partitions_in_table,
    SUM(CASE WHEN pruning_verdict = 'SCAN_CANDIDATE' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS partitions_scanned,
    SUM(CASE WHEN pruning_verdict = 'METADATA_PRUNED' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS partitions_pruned,
    SUM(CASE WHEN pruning_verdict = 'SCAN_CANDIDATE' THEN row_count ELSE 0 END) AS rows_scanned_by_warehouse,
    SUM(CASE WHEN pruning_verdict = 'METADATA_PRUNED' THEN row_count ELSE 0 END) AS rows_avoided_by_pruning,
    ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN pruning_verdict = 'METADATA_PRUNED' THEN row_count ELSE 0 END) / SUM(row_count), 2) AS pruning_efficiency_pct
FROM optimizer_pruning_decision;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 1
-- ASSERT: COL[total_partitions_in_table] = 4
-- ASSERT: COL[partitions_scanned] = 1
-- ASSERT: COL[partitions_pruned] = 3

title: #089 Detecting Distribution Skew In Parallel Shards
description: Write an enterprise DBA audit query that calculates the distribution of rows across distributed worker shards. Compute the mean shard row count, calculate the percentage variance from the mean, and flag any shard operating above 150% of the cluster average as a CRITICAL_STRAGGLER_HAZARD.

-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Diagnostic query identifying straggler nodes via statistical variance
WITH cluster_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        AVG(row_count) AS avg_shard_rows,
        SUM(row_count) AS total_cluster_rows
    FROM mpp_shard_telemetry
)
SELECT 
    s.shard_id,
    s.worker_host,
    s.row_count,
    ROUND(100.0 * s.row_count / c.total_cluster_rows, 2) AS pct_of_total_cluster_rows,
    ROUND(1.0 * s.row_count / c.avg_shard_rows, 2) AS skew_multiplier_vs_mean,
    CASE 
        WHEN s.row_count > 1.5 * c.avg_shard_rows THEN 'CRITICAL_STRAGGLER_HAZARD'
        ELSE 'BALANCED_DISTRIBUTION'
    END AS shard_health_status
FROM mpp_shard_telemetry s
CROSS JOIN cluster_metrics c
ORDER BY s.row_count DESC;

-- ASSERT: COL[skew_multiplier_vs_mean] = 2.49

title: #090 Distributed Key Salting For Skewed Joins
description: Implement two-phase key salting in SQL for a 4-way salt split on skewed customer 0. Join the salted fact and dimension tables, proving that all transactions join correctly without data loss or skew hotspots.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Two-Phase Key Salting Join Pipeline
WITH salted_fact AS (
    SELECT 
        order_id,
        customer_id,
        order_amount_usd,
        CASE 
            WHEN customer_id = 0 THEN customer_id || '_' || (order_id % 4)
            ELSE customer_id || '_0'
        END AS salted_join_key
    FROM fact_orders_skewed
),
salted_dimension AS (
    -- Explode ONLY the skewed customer 0 across 4 salts [0, 1, 2, 3]
    SELECT 
        c.customer_id,
        c.customer_type,
        c.customer_id || '_' || s.salt AS salted_join_key
    FROM dim_customers_salted c
    CROSS JOIN (
        SELECT 0 AS salt UNION ALL 
        SELECT 1 UNION ALL 
        SELECT 2 UNION ALL 
        SELECT 3
    ) s
    WHERE c.customer_id = 0
    
    UNION ALL
    
    -- Keep non-skewed keys with static salt _0
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        customer_type,
        customer_id || '_0' AS salted_join_key
    FROM dim_customers_salted
    WHERE customer_id != 0
)
SELECT 
    f.order_id,
    f.customer_id,
    d.customer_type,
    f.salted_join_key,
    f.order_amount_usd,
    'SALTED_HASH_JOIN_SUCCESS' AS execution_plan_step
FROM salted_fact f
INNER JOIN salted_dimension d ON f.salted_join_key = d.salted_join_key
ORDER BY f.order_id ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 5
-- ASSERT: COL[order_id] = 1001
-- ASSERT: COL[salted_join_key] = 0_1
-- ASSERT: COL[customer_type] = GUEST_CHECKOUT_HOTSPOT\n
notes: Engines: Databricks Spark SQL, Snowflake, BigQuery, PostgreSQL, DuckDB, SQLite
Module: MPP And Cloud Warehouses
Source: sql-handbook/exercises/09_mpp_and_cloud_warehouses/090_distributed_key_salting_for_skewed_joins.sql
use_case: Distributed Join Skew Mitigation & Two-Phase Key Salting Pattern. When joining a massive fact table (orders) with a dimension table (customers): - Unregistered guest checkouts share a single key: `customer_id = 0` (or `NULL`). - If 60% of all orders belong to customer 0, a standard distributed hash join sends all customer 0 records to a single worker partition. That worker crashes with Executor OutOfMemory (OOM Exit Code 137). The Production Two-Phase Salting Pattern: 1. Fact side: Append a salt modulo $S \in [0..K-1]$ to the skewed key: `customer_id || '_' || (order_id % K)`. Non-skewed keys append `_0`. 2. Dimension side: Replicate ONLY the skewed customer key $K$ times with suffixes `_0`, `_1`, ..., `_K-1`. Normal customer keys keep suffix `_0`. 3. Join on the salted key: The skewed key is now evenly distributed across $K$ workers!

title: #091 Broadcast Vs Shuffle Join Thresholds
description: Model a cost-based optimizer catalog with table statistics. Write a query that inspects table size metadata against a 10MB (10,485,760 bytes) threshold and chooses the optimal join execution strategy between BHJ and Shuffle Sort-Merge Join.
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Planner cost simulation: Determine physical join strategy for fact_web_impressions
SELECT 
    f.table_name AS fact_table,
    d.table_name AS dim_table,
    d.total_bytes AS dim_size_bytes,
    10485760 AS broadcast_threshold_bytes,
    CASE 
        WHEN d.total_bytes <= 10485760 THEN 'BROADCAST_HASH_JOIN'
        ELSE 'SHUFFLE_SORT_MERGE_JOIN'
    END AS selected_physical_join_strategy,
    CASE 
        WHEN d.total_bytes <= 10485760 THEN 'ZERO_NETWORK_SHUFFLE_OPTIMAL'
        ELSE 'NETWORK_SHUFFLE_EXCHANGE_REQUIRED'
    END AS execution_tradeoff
FROM query_planner_table_stats f
CROSS JOIN query_planner_table_stats d
WHERE f.table_type = 'FACT' AND d.table_type = 'DIMENSION'
ORDER BY d.total_bytes ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 2
-- ASSERT: COL[dim_table] = dim_ad_categories
-- ASSERT: COL[selected_physical_join_strategy] = BROADCAST_HASH_JOIN
-- ASSERT: COL[execution_tradeoff] = ZERO_NETWORK_SHUFFLE_OPTIMAL\n

Module: MPP And Cloud Warehouses

use_case: Distributed Query Planner & Physical Join Strategy Selection. When joining a 500GB Fact Table to a lookup Dimension Table: 1. Broadcast Hash Join (BHJ / Map-Side Join): If the dimension table is smaller than the broadcast threshold (e.g. 10MB in Spark, configured via `spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold`), the driver transmits a copy of the dimension to every executor. Fact partitions are processed locally with ZERO network shuffle! 2. Shuffle Hash Join (SHJ) / Sort-Merge Join (SMJ): If the dimension exceeds the threshold, both tables must be hashed and shuffled across all cluster nodes over the physical network.

title: #096 Incident The 99 Percent Straggler Task Disaster
description: SURGICAL TRIAGE & REMEDIATION: Two-Path Execution Architecture: 1. Filter valid non-null customer keys: Join them against customer dimension with zero skew. 2. Direct pass-through stream: Process NULL/Guest checkouts separately with default attributes, bypassing the customer dimension join entirely. 3. UNION ALL the two streams. This eliminates join shuffle skew and restores parallel execution!
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Production recovery: Two-Path execution eliminating NULL shuffle hotspot
WITH authenticated_orders AS (
    -- Path 1: Join only valid customer keys (no NULL skew)
    SELECT 
        t.txn_id,
        t.customer_id,
        c.customer_tier,
        c.country_code,
        t.amount_usd,
        'AUTHENTICATED_JOIN' AS processing_path
    FROM incident_raw_transactions t
    INNER JOIN incident_dim_customers c ON t.customer_id = c.customer_id
    WHERE t.customer_id IS NOT NULL
),
unassigned_guest_orders AS (
    -- Path 2: Direct bypass of dimension join for NULL keys
    SELECT 
        t.txn_id,
        'GUEST_USER' AS customer_id,
        'UNASSIGNED' AS customer_tier,
        'UNKNOWN'    AS country_code,
        t.amount_usd,
        'DIRECT_GUEST_BYPASS' AS processing_path
    FROM incident_raw_transactions t
    WHERE t.customer_id IS NULL
)
SELECT * FROM authenticated_orders
UNION ALL
SELECT * FROM unassigned_guest_orders
ORDER BY txn_id ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---
-- ASSERT: ROW_COUNT = 5
-- ASSERT: COL[txn_id] = TXN-101
-- ASSERT: COL[customer_tier] = ENTERPRISE
-- ASSERT: COL[processing_path] = AUTHENTICATED_JOIN\n

title: #098 Incident Out Of Order Cdc Timeline Corruption
description: SURGICAL TRIAGE & REMEDIATION: Execute a deterministic SQL self-healing reconciliation pipeline using window functions (`LEAD` and `ROW_NUMBER`) over the true source event timestamp (`event_timestamp`), reconstructing seamless, non-overlapping SCD Type 2 intervals (`valid_from`, `valid_to`, `is_current`).
code:
-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Self-healing deterministic timeline reconstruction query
WITH sequenced_cdc_events AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        address_line,
        state_code,
        event_timestamp AS valid_from,
        COALESCE(
            LEAD(event_timestamp) OVER (
                PARTITION BY customer_id 
                ORDER BY event_timestamp ASC
            ),
            '9999-12-31 23:59:59'
        ) AS valid_to,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY customer_id 
            ORDER BY event_timestamp DESC
        ) AS recency_rank
    FROM raw_corrupted_cdc_events
)
SELECT 
    customer_id,
    address_line,
    state_code,
    valid_from,
    valid_to,
    CASE WHEN recency_rank = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS is_current,
    'DETERMINISTIC_SELF_HEALING_SCD2_REPAIRED' AS audit_status
FROM sequenced_cdc_events
ORDER BY valid_from ASC;

-- --- [VERIFICATION / ASSERTION] ---

-- ASSERT: COL[customer_id] = CUST-101
-- ASSERT: COL[valid_from] = 2024-06-01 10:00:00
-- ASSERT: COL[valid_to] = 2024-06-01 10:05:00

title: #099 Incident Accidental Cartesian Tempdb Exhaustion
description: SURGICAL TRIAGE & REMEDIATION: Pre-deduplicate the dimensional side using a CTE with deterministic tie-breaking: `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY promo_code ORDER BY effective_timestamp DESC)` Filter strictly `WHERE rn = 1` before performing the join, guaranteeing a strict 1:1 join grain.

-- --- [SOLUTION QUERY] ---
-- Production recovery: Pre-deduplicate dimension to guarantee 1:1 join grain
WITH unique_dim_promotions AS (
    SELECT 
        promo_code,
        discount_pct,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY promo_code 
            ORDER BY created_at DESC
        ) AS dedupe_rank
    FROM non_unique_promotions
)
SELECT 
    o.order_id,
    o.customer_id,
    o.promo_code,
    o.gross_order_usd,
    p.discount_pct AS applied_discount_pct,
    ROUND(o.gross_order_usd * (1.0 - p.discount_pct / 100.0), 2) AS net_discounted_usd,
    'CARTESIAN_PREVENTED_1_TO_1_GRAIN' AS join_safety_status
FROM incident_fact_orders o
INNER JOIN unique_dim_promotions p 
    ON o.promo_code = p.promo_code 
   AND p.dedupe_rank = 1
ORDER BY o.order_id ASC;

-- ASSERT: COL[order_id] = ORD-5001
-- ASSERT: COL[applied_discount_pct] = 15.0

    FROM gold_sales_facts f
    LEFT JOIN gold_dim_customers c ON f.customer_id = c.customer_id
    WHERE c.customer_id IS NULL
),
pillar_3_nullity_mandate AS (
    SELECT 
        '3. Nullity Mandate' AS test_name,
        CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 'PASS' ELSE 'FAIL' END AS test_status
    FROM gold_sales_facts
    WHERE sale_id IS NULL OR customer_id IS NULL OR net_billed_usd IS NULL OR sale_date IS NULL
),
pillar_4_numeric_bounds AS (
    SELECT 
        '4. Numeric Bounds Sanity' AS test_name,
        CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 'PASS' ELSE 'FAIL' END AS test_status
    FROM gold_sales_facts
    WHERE gross_amount_usd <= 0.00 OR discount_usd < 0.00 OR net_billed_usd <= 0.00
),
pillar_5_temporal_sanity AS (
    SELECT 
        '5. Temporal Sanity' AS test_name,
        CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 'PASS' ELSE 'FAIL' END AS test_status
    FROM gold_sales_facts
    WHERE sale_date > '2099-12-31' OR sale_date < '2020-01-01'
),
pillar_6_financial_invariance AS (
    SELECT 
        '6. Financial Reconciliation Invariant' AS test_name,
        CASE WHEN COUNT(*) = 0 THEN 'PASS' ELSE 'FAIL' END AS test_status
    FROM gold_sales_facts
    WHERE (gross_amount_usd - discount_usd) != net_billed_usd
)
SELECT test_name, test_status FROM pillar_1_uniqueness
UNION ALL SELECT test_name, test_status FROM pillar_2_referential_integrity
UNION ALL SELECT test_name, test_status FROM pillar_3_nullity_mandate
UNION ALL SELECT test_name, test_status FROM pillar_4_numeric_bounds
UNION ALL SELECT test_name, test_status FROM pillar_5_temporal_sanity
UNION ALL SELECT test_name, test_status FROM pillar_6_financial_invariance
ORDER BY test_name ASC;
